question.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

Using the chain rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({cos}^{2}⁡(3x-{y}^{2})) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-{y}^{2})\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-{y}^{2})) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-{y}^{2})\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-{y}^{2}))\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(3x-{y}^{2}) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-{y}^{2})\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-{y}^{2}))\cdot 3 \\  & =-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-{y}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-{y}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$
